title: Wedding Guest Outfit Ideas: Why a Royal Blue Anarkali Is Always the Right Answer
excerpt: Not too bridal, never underdressed: why a flowy royal blue georgette Anarkali works so well for wedding guests, plus three ways to style it for every event.
body:
Choosing a wedding guest outfit is a balancing act: you want to look beautiful in every photo, but you never want to compete with the bride. A flowy Anarkali in a rich jewel tone solves this every time – and royal blue might be the most flattering of them all.

## Why royal blue works at every wedding

- **It suits most skin tones.** Royal blue brightens fair skin and looks rich on wheatish and deeper skin.
- **It rarely clashes with the bride.** Brides usually wear red, pink or pastels, so blue keeps you elegant and distinct.
- **It photographs beautifully** in both daylight and evening lights.

## How to style it for each function

| Function | Jewellery | Shoes | Hair |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sangeet | Kundan jhumkas | Block heels | Loose curls |
| Wedding ceremony | Statement earrings + maang tikka | Pearl heels | Low bun with flowers |
| Reception | Polki or gold drop earrings | Metallic heels | Sleek side part |

## 3 ways to drape the dupatta

1. **One shoulder:** pin it on the left shoulder and let it fall – easy and graceful.
2. **Both arms:** drape across your back and over both elbows – perfect for photos.
3. **Classic front:** let it fall evenly over both shoulders for a traditional look.

## One Anarkali, three looks

Royal blue is rich enough for an evening wedding and calm enough for a day event, so one Anarkali can carry you through a whole wedding season. Keep the outfit and change only the jewellery, dupatta, hair and shoes.

| Look | Jewellery | Dupatta | Hair | Shoes | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classic festive | Gold jhumkas, bangles | Both shoulders | Low bun with flowers | Embellished juttis | Wedding, Diwali, Eid |
| Modern minimal | Silver studs, cocktail ring | One shoulder, pinned | Sleek ponytail or bun | Strappy heels | Cocktail, New Year's Eve |
| Winter daytime | Pearl drops | Around the neck | Loose waves | Juttis, ankle boots outside | Family lunch, Christmas |

### Look 1: Classic festive

The full traditional look. Drape the gota lace dupatta over both shoulders so the border frames the outfit, then add gold jhumkas, a stack of bangles and a small bindi. A low bun with fresh flowers or a gajra finishes it. Royal blue stands out next to the reds and pinks at most weddings, so this look photographs well in group pictures. Our guide to [jewellery to wear with an Anarkali](/blog/jewellery-to-wear-with-an-anarkali/) explains how to match earrings to the neckline.

### Look 2: Modern minimal

For a cocktail party or New Year's Eve, strip it back. Pin the dupatta neatly over one shoulder, swap gold for silver or diamond-look studs and a single cocktail ring, and wear your hair in a sleek ponytail or high bun. Strappy heels, a metallic clutch and a berry or red lip turn the same Anarkali into an evening gown.

### Look 3: Winter daytime

For a Christmas lunch, a family visit or a daytime puja in cold weather, go soft and practical. Wrap the dupatta loosely around your neck like a scarf, add pearl drops and minimal makeup, and leave your hair in loose waves. Outside, wear a long camel or black coat and ankle boots, then change into juttis indoors. A grey or cream wool shawl looks lovely against royal blue.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Georgette has a slightly grainy surface that softens the light, so royal blue looks deep rather than shiny in photos. It also recovers well from creasing: hang it in a steamy bathroom for ten minutes after travel, and most creases fall out.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is georgette comfortable for long events?**
Yes – georgette is light and flowy, and the Anarkali is lined for comfort.

**How should I store an Anarkali with gota lace?**
Fold it with tissue paper between the layers and keep it in a cotton bag. Dry clean only.

**What jewellery goes with a royal blue Anarkali?**
Gold, silver, pearls and kundan all work. Gold feels traditional, silver feels modern, and pearls look soft for daytime.

**What colour dupatta goes with a royal blue Anarkali?**
The matching gota lace dupatta is the easiest choice. For contrast, try silver, soft pink or mustard.

**Can I wear a royal blue Anarkali to a day event?**
Yes. Keep the jewellery light, wear the dupatta around your neck and choose soft makeup and loose hair.
